architecture.title: Intel, 8080/8085 Assembly Language Programming Manual
architecture.note: Chapter 1, especially pp. 1-5–1-16: registers, flags, stack, I/O and addressing. Instruction descriptions distinguish 8080 from 8085 operations.

compatibility.title: Zilog, Z80 CPU User Manual, UM008011-0816
compatibility.note: Architectural overview and instruction/flag descriptions; a later manufacturer manual, used for Z80 behaviour rather than an 8080 launch date. https://www.zilog.com/docs/z80/um0080.pdf

architecture.title: Motorola, M6800 Programming Reference Manual, M68PRM(D)
architecture.note: Register model, addressing modes, stack and interrupt operation; original 6800, not the later 6809.

architecture.title: Motorola, MC6800 8-Bit Microprocessing Unit data sheet
architecture.note: 16-bit address bus, two accumulators and external memory interface. https://console5.com/techwiki/images/f/fc/MC6800.pdf

system.title: Southwest Technical Products Corporation, 6800 Computer System brochure
system.note: Contemporary system maker’s description of the processor board, bus, memory and I/O. Circa 1975 date is archival, not treated as a precise publication date. https://www.hartetechnologies.com/manuals/SWTPC/6800%20Computer%20System/6800_Computer_System_Brochure.pdf

display.title: MOS Technology, 6560/6561 Video Interface Chip data sheet
display.note: February 1980 issue; pp. 1–2 visually inspected: NTSC/PAL variants, video matrix, character and colour pointers, sound generators. https://www.zimmers.net/anonftp/pub/cbm/documents/chipdata/6560.zip

display.title: Commodore, VIC-20 Programmer’s Reference Guide
display.note: The VIC chip and memory maps; distinguishes the machine’s normal character display from the chip’s programmable settings. First edition, sixth printing.

function.title: Motorola, SN74LS783/MC6883 and SN74LS785 Synchronous Address Multiplexer
function.note: ADI-595R2, 1984 copyright: original scan visually inspected; system block diagram, RAM addressing, clock-rate and video-offset controls. Document date is not a chip introduction date. https://maltedmedia.com/6809/Sheets/Data/MC6883.pdf

function.title: Duncan Smeed and Ian Sommerville, Inside the Dragon
function.note: 1983, pp. 154–157, 162, 171–172: SAM, video and SAMMOD in the Dragon; the rate and display consequences depend on mode.

architecture.title: Nintendo, SNES Development Manual, Book I
architecture.note: Sections 2-22 and 3: sound CPU, DSP, 64KB memory, four communication ports, BRR blocks and echo warnings. Original manual at https://floating.muncher.se/bot/manual/book1_text.pdf

corroboration.title: SNESdev, S-SMP technical documentation
corroboration.note: Modern hardware-research documentation: distinguishes S-SMP, SPC700 core, S-DSP and shared RAM. https://snes.nesdev.org/wiki/S-SMP

architecture.title: Texas Instruments, TMS9918A/TMS9928A/TMS9929A Video Display Processors Data Manual
architecture.note: November 1982; CPU interface, display modes, pattern tables and sprite evaluation. Graphics II is an A-series feature; do not attribute all A-series modes to the original non-A part.

mode_4.title: Sega, Software Reference Manual for the Sega Mark III Console
mode_4.note: VDP section, pp. 6–10, visually inspected: 16KB VRAM, tile-map attributes, palette banks, scroll locks and eight sprites per line. https://segaretro.org/images/d/d6/SoftwareReferenceManualForSegaMarkIIIEU.pdf

mode_4.title: Charles MacDonald, SMS VDP Documentation
mode_4.note: First-hand technical investigation, 12 November 2002: Mode 4, ports, patterns and revision distinctions. https://www.smspower.org/uploads/Development/msvdp-20021112.txt

operation.title: Texas Instruments, SN76489AN digital complex sound generator data sheet
operation.note: Original scan visually inspected, pp. 1–3: three tone generators, 10-bit periods, attenuation, noise and latched interface. https://map.grauw.nl/resources/sound/texas_instruments_sn76489an.pdf

operation.title: Maxim and SMS Power contributors, SN76489
operation.note: Hardware investigation and implementation comparisons: latch/data format, machine ports and variant differences. https://www.smspower.org/Development/SN76489

architecture.title: Sega, Genesis Software Manual
architecture.note: February 1992 revision: Mode V, pattern-name tables, window, sprites and DMA. Public editions catalogued at https://techdocs.exodusemulator.com/Console/SegaMegaDrive/Documentation.html

behaviour.title: Charles MacDonald, Sega Genesis VDP Documentation, version 1.5f
behaviour.note: Original hardware investigation preserved in transcription: window replaces plane A; external DMA stops 68000, unlike VRAM fill/copy. Early 315-5313 is not every later board’s part number. https://www.neperos.com/article/picoxo1fc33c8979

operation.title: MOS Technology, MCS6522 Versatile Interface Adapter preliminary data sheet
operation.note: November 1977: two bidirectional ports, data-direction registers, timer modes, shift register and interrupt flags. Original text and scan archive at https://www.zimmers.net/anonftp/pub/cbm/documents/chipdata/6522-VIA.txt

operation.title: Andrew Bray, Adrian Dickens and Mark Holmes, The Advanced User Guide for the BBC Microcomputer
operation.note: Chapter 22: general VIA operation and the different wiring of the BBC’s system and user VIAs. Chapter text inspected; use machine-specific address map rather than a universal VIA address.

operation.title: Atari, De Re Atari
operation.note: Chapters 2–6 and Appendix E: ANTIC modes, DMA, display-list interrupts, player/missile priority and GTIA modes. Preface credits Kathleen Pitta with Appendix E. https://www.atariarchives.org/dere/

context.title: Lee H. Pappas, An interview with Doug Neubauer, ANALOG Computing 47
context.note: October 1986, pp. 89–90: retrospective participant account of the Atari chipset, including GTIA’s earlier design and production timing. Used for context, not register specifications.

architecture.title: VLSI Technology, Acorn RISC Machine (ARM) Family Data Manual
architecture.note: 1990, VL86C010 CPU description and programmer’s model: 32-bit arithmetic, load/store, sixteen visible registers, barrel shifter and 26-bit addressing. https://acorn.huininga.nl/pub/docs/datasheets/ARM/

people.title: Arm, A brief history of Arm, part 1
people.note: Manufacturer’s historical account credits Sophie Wilson’s instruction-set work and Steve Furber’s chip design; early work at Acorn and 1985 first silicon. https://developer.arm.com/community/arm-community-blogs/b/architectures-and-processors-blog/posts/a-brief-history-of-arm-part-1

people.title: Computer History Museum, Sophie Wilson, 2012 Fellow
people.note: Institutional profile corroborates co-design with Furber and Archimedes use. https://computerhistory.org/profile/sophie-wilson/

function.title: Motorola, MC6845 CRT Controller data sheet
function.note: Original part: programmable timing, memory/raster address outputs, display enable, cursor and light-pen capture. https://archive.decromancer.ca/bitsavers.org/components/motorola/_dataSheets/6845.pdf

function.title: Andrew Bray, Adrian Dickens and Mark Holmes, The Advanced User Guide for the BBC Microcomputer
function.note: Chapter 18: CRTC, screen layouts and the BBC’s other video circuitry. Distinguishes machine wiring from the chip’s own outputs.

sound.title: Atari, De Re Atari
sound.note: Chapter 7: audio frequency/control registers, distortion, volume and joined 16-bit frequency options. https://www.atariarchives.org/dere/

design.title: Lee H. Pappas, An interview with Doug Neubauer, ANALOG Computing 47
design.note: Participant interview, October 1986, pp. 89–90: Neubauer’s POKEY design work, initial keyboard/audio/paddle scope, serial addition and audio enhancements.

interface.title: Commodore, Commodore 128 Programmer’s Reference Guide
interface.note: Chapter 10, pp. 292–334, particularly pp. 304–313: private 16KB video RAM, indexed D600/D601 access, ready bit, attributes, block write/copy. https://www.zimmers.net/anonftp/pub/cbm/manuals/c128/C128_Programmers_Reference_Guide.pdf

interface.title: Commodore, Commodore 128 System Guide
interface.note: 1985 guide: separate 40/80-column outputs and system modes. Same publisher, complementary coverage rather than independent corroboration. https://www.zimmers.net/anonftp/pub/cbm/manuals/c128/C128_System_Guide.pdf

operation.title: Atari/GCC, Atari 7800 Software Guide
operation.note: Display list, Display List List, zones, indirect graphics and line-RAM/DMA sections. Preserved technical guide: https://atarihq.com/danb/files/7800%20Software%20Guide.pdf

architecture.title: Motorola, DSP56000 24-Bit Digital Signal Processor Family Manual
architecture.note: Core data ALU and addressing descriptions: 24-bit operands, 48-bit product, 56-bit accumulators and X/Y data spaces. Later family manual; features added to later family members are not assigned to DSP56001. https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/DSP56000UM.pdf

falcon.title: Atari, Falcon030 Owner’s Manual
falcon.note: C302952-001 Rev B, January 1993 printing: 68030, DSP56001 and separate audio features. https://www.atarimania.com/documents/Atari-Falcon030-Owners-Manual.pdf

falcon.title: Atari, Falcon030 Service Guide
falcon.note: C303062-001, 1 October 1992: DSP and audio hardware, including 16-bit stereo conversion. https://archive.org/details/Atari_Falcon030_Service_Guide_1992-10-01
